233	## Available scripts
234	
235	- **`scripts/check-daemon.sh`** — Single-shot daemon health + version + log-dir check, with optional auto-start. Outputs JSON to stdout.
236	  - Flags: `--start`, `--json` (default on), `--help`.
237	  - Exit: `0` healthy, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable, `4` client/daemon version mismatch.
238	- **`scripts/submit.sh`** — Submit ONE task, return clean JSON `{task_id, group, label, after, ...}`. Wraps `pueue add --print-task-id` with defensive id parsing. Auto-creates the group if missing.
239	  - Flags: `--label`, `--group`, `--after` (repeatable), `--immediate`, `--stashed`, `--delay`, `--priority`, `--working-dir`, `--escape`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
240	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` `pueue add` failed, `4` daemon unreachable.
241	- **`scripts/wait.py`** — Block until selected tasks reach terminal status; emit a JSON summary. Selectors: `--ids`, `--label`, `--label-prefix`, `--group`. Quiet by default — emits only one initial line + state-change events on stderr; pass `--verbose` for per-tick output.
242	  - Flags: `--ids`, `--label` (repeatable), `--label-prefix`, `--group`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds`, `--fail-fast`, `--verbose`, `--help`.
243	  - Exit: `0` all succeeded, `1` arg error, `4` daemon unreachable, `5` ≥1 failed/killed/dependency-failed, `6` timeout.
244	- **`scripts/submit-dag.py`** — Declarative DAG submitter. Reads YAML or JSON (file path or `-` for stdin), topo-sorts, validates, submits with wired `--after`, returns `{name → id, topo_order, width_per_group, isolated_group?}`. Computes DAG fan-out width per group; with `--isolated-group [NAME]` creates a fresh dedicated group sized to the width (preferred — leaves user's other groups untouched). With `--auto-parallel` mutates target groups in place. Without either, only warns.
245	  - Flags: `--format`, `--default-group`, `--label-prefix`, `--dry-run`, `--print-graph`, `--auto-parallel`, `--isolated-group [NAME]`, `--help`.
246	  - Exit: `0` all submitted, `1` schema/cycle/unknown-ref/conflicting flags, `2` pueue not installed, `3` mid-run pueue failure (stdout still emits IDs that DID submit, for cleanup).
247	- **`scripts/cleanup.sh`** — Prune pueue task history, empty groups, and old log files. Wraps `pueue clean` + `pueue group remove` for empty non-default groups + optional log-file mtime pruning. Emits a JSON report. Run weekly to keep `pueue status --json` fast.
248	  - Flags: `--successful-only`, `--group GROUP`, `--remove-empty-groups`, `--logs-older-than N`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
249	  - Exit: `0` ok (or dry-run), `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable.
250	
251	## Bundled assets
252	
253	- `assets/dag.example.yaml` — 5-task fan-out/fan-in (`fetch → featurize → {train_a, train_b} → evaluate`). Pass it to `submit-dag.py` with `--dry-run` first to see the topo order.
254	- `assets/pueue.yml.example` — Config snippet showing `pause_group_on_failure: true`, `default_parallel_tasks`, and a sample `groups:` block. The header comment names the platform-specific destination paths.
255	
256	## Reference files
257	
258	- `references/cli-cheatsheet.md` — Read **when** the task needs `pueue follow`, `pueue log`, `pueue restart`, `pueue kill`, `pueue clean`, `pueue group/parallel`, `pueue pause/start`, `pueue reset`, `pueue edit`, `pueue env`, or any other un-wrapped `pueue` subcommand. Has a one-line "when to use" for each.
259	- `references/json-schema.md` — Read **when** writing custom `jq` queries against `pueue status --json` or `pueue log --json`, or when a script's JSON parsing surprises you. Documents the observed schema on pueue 4.0.2 with concrete examples for each status variant.
260	- `references/dag-patterns.md` — Read **when** the user asks for shapes beyond fan-out/fan-in (mixed sequential+parallel, diamond, etc.) or hits the AND-only / success-only limitation. Has examples and a "when to escalate to a real orchestrator" decision table.
261	- `references/daemon-and-config.md` — Read **when** setting up `pueued` for the first time, configuring per-OS paths, picking config knobs (`pause_group_on_failure`, `default_parallel_tasks`), or wiring up launchd / systemd-user.
262	
263	## Gotchas
264	
265	- **DAG fan-out is gated by `parallel_tasks` per group.** Even when two siblings both depend only on `A` and the DAG allows them to run in parallel, they will *serialize* if their group's `parallel_tasks=1`. Pueue's parallelism primitive is the group, not the dependency graph. `submit-dag.py` warns when DAG width exceeds the group's slots and suggests the exact `pueue parallel N --group G` command; pass `--auto-parallel` to apply it.
266	- **`pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does not preserve quoting.** Pueue joins all `<COMMAND>` args and re-shells. The single-quoted `'sleep 60'` is unwrapped by *your* shell before pueue sees it, then pueue re-splits. Quote the **whole** command as one arg: `pueue add 'sleep 60'` or `submit.sh -- 'bash -c "sleep 60 && echo done"'`.
267	- **`--after` is AND-only and success-only.** Failed parent → dependent's `status.Done.result` becomes `"DependencyFailed"` and it never runs. There is no OR, no run-on-failure, no retry-on-failure. If you need that, you need a real orchestrator.
268	- **Pueue does NOT auto-create groups.** `pueue add --group new_name` exits 1 with `"Group new_name doesn't exists. Use one of these: [...]"`. `submit.sh` calls `pueue group add` first if the group is missing.
269	- **`pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW task id.** The old id stays in history with its result. To retry in-place (reusing the id, overwriting the log), pass `--in-place`. Choose deliberately — agent users often want `--in-place` for "retry this".
270	- **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-only, no CLI flag.** Set it in `pueue.yml`; reload with `pueue reset` or restart `pueued`.
271	- **Logs live in platform-specific dirs**, not your CWD. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/logs/`. Linux: `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/`. Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\logs\`. `pueue log --json --full <id>` reads them for you.
272	- **`pueue wait` returns 0 even if the waited-on tasks failed.** It blocks until terminal, period. To know success/failure, query `pueue status --json` afterward (or use `wait.py`, which does this for you and returns a non-zero exit on failures).
273	- **`pueue remove` requires each id as a separate positional arg** (not a space-joined string from a subshell). Use bash arrays: `IDS=($(...)) && pueue remove "${IDS[@]}"`.
274	- **`pueue clean --successful-only` is a flag, not the default.** Plain `pueue clean` removes ALL finished tasks (including failures, which you may want to keep for debugging). Be deliberate.
275	- **`pueue add --print-task-id` writes the bare integer to stdout.** No JSON, no prose. `submit.sh` parses with a regex that tolerates future format changes; if you bypass `submit.sh`, capture with `ID=$(pueue add --print-task-id ... )` directly.
276
```

```text
58	## Authoring Mode: Design Verifiable Surfaces
59	
60	Every CLI/tool/service surface you add must satisfy this checklist:
61	
62	1. **`--help` is mandatory.** Show usage, every flag, examples, and exit
63	   codes. The agent (and the next human) reads this first.
64	2. **`--dry-run` for any side effect.** File writes, network calls, database
65	   mutations, config edits, deploys, restarts. Dry-run must still load the
66	   real config and resolve the real plan, not short-circuit before parsing.
67	3. **`--print-config` / `--show-config` for config-loading programs.** Print
68	   the fully resolved config (after env/file/CLI merging) so the user can
69	   diff what the program actually sees vs. what they edited.
70	4. **Isolated-state smoke entrypoint.** The tool must accept `--config <path>`
71	   and respect `$HOME` / `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` overrides; never hard-code
72	   `~/.foo`. This lets `env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) ...` exercise the real load
73	   path with zero blast radius.
74	5. **Explicit exit-code contract.** `0` for success; non-zero for failure
75	   classes (`1` runtime/user error, `2` usage error is a common convention).
76	   Document the codes in `--help`.
77	6. **Structured stdout, diagnostics on stderr.** Stdout is the program's
78	   data output (parseable when reasonable). Logs, progress, and errors go
79	   to stderr so callers can pipe stdout safely.
80	7. **Self-verification after authoring.** Before declaring done, run:
81	   `cmd --help`, `cmd --dry-run <smallest input>`, `cmd --print-config`
82	   (if applicable), an intentionally-bad input to confirm non-zero exit,
83	   and one isolated-state smoke (`env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) ...`).
84	
85	See `references/authoring-checklist.md` for concrete templates per
86	language (Python tyro/click, Node commander/yargs, Bash).
87	
88	## Verification Mode: Verification Ladder
89	
90	Pick the highest safe rung that exercises the actual failure mode. Do not
91	stop at a lower rung when the next harmless rung exists.
92	
93	1. **Syntax/schema gate** — `yamllint`, `jsonschema`, `ansible-playbook
94	   --syntax-check`, `terraform validate`, `docker compose config`,
95	   `mkdocs build`, `tsc --noEmit`.
96	2. **Rendered/applied config gate** — render templates and generated files,
97	   then validate those outputs. For chezmoi, inspect `chezmoi diff`,
98	   `chezmoi apply --dry-run --verbose`, or `chezmoi execute-template`; do
99	   not validate only the `.tmpl` source.
100	3. **App/tool-native loader gate** — prefer the command the app itself
101	   exposes: `config check`, `doctor`, `debug`, `--print-config`,
102	   `--show-config`, `--dry-run`, `--check`, `validate`, `plan`, or a small
103	   script that imports and loads the same config module used at startup.
104	4. **Compile/build gate** — when config influences generated code, bundling,
105	   routing, plugins, import paths, or type definitions, run the narrowest
106	   compile/build that loads it.
107	5. **Harmless runtime smoke** — for runtime-only failures, run the narrowest
108	   local smoke with isolated state: `/tmp`, temp `$HOME`, temp config path,
109	   temp database/file store, local container, `--check`, `--dry-run`,
110	   limited tag, limited target, or loopback-only service.
111	
112	Record which rung you reached. If you cannot reach the app-native loader or
113	runtime smoke safely, say so explicitly and explain what is still untested.
114	
115	See `references/config-examples.md` for concrete commands per ecosystem
116	(Ansible, chezmoi, JS/TS, Python settings, Docker Compose, Kubernetes,
117	Terraform/OpenTofu, generic loaders).
118	
119	## Default Workflow
120	
121	1. Identify which mode applies. Authoring (new surface) and verification
122	   (changed surface) often co-occur — handle both.
123	2. **Authoring**: walk the 7-point checklist above. Stub out missing items
124	   before the change is "done."
125	3. **Verification**: list the minimum ladder for this change, then run the
126	   lowest cheap gate first and continue until the highest harmless gate has
127	   passed.
128	4. When a gate fails, fix the cause and re-run all earlier affected gates.
129	5. Summarize the exact commands and the highest gate passed.
130	
131	## Ansible Rule
132	
133	`ansible-playbook --syntax-check` is only the first step. It does not execute
134	tasks, evaluate all runtime conditions, contact targets, validate module side
135	effects, or prove variables are correct for the selected hosts. If a
136	playbook, role, inventory, or variable change can fail at execution time, run
137	the narrowest relevant smoke: `--check`, `--diff`, `--tags`, `--skip-tags`,
138	`--limit`, localhost/container inventory, or a role-specific test harness.
139	
140	## Gotchas
141	
142	- **A surface without `--dry-run` is a surface you cannot rehearse.** When
143	  authoring, add it before the destructive code path, not after.
144	- **`--help` must list exit codes and side effects.** "What does this
145	  command do?" should be answerable without reading source.
146	- **Validate rendered config, not just source templates.** Template syntax
147	  can pass while the rendered file has invalid paths, missing env vars,
148	  duplicate keys, or host-specific values the app rejects.
149	- **The app's own loader is the authority.** Generic YAML/JSON/TOML parsing
150	  does not catch semantic errors such as unsupported keys, wrong plugin
151	  names, invalid enum values, env interpolation bugs, or changed default
152	  paths.
```

1	---
2	name: clash-proxy-api
3	description: Inspect and control a local or configured Clash/mihomo external-controller API, especially the common 127.0.0.1:9090 controller paired with HTTP proxy port 7890 and SOCKS port 7891. Use when the user asks to check the current Clash node, switch proxy groups between named nodes such as Hanru/David, test node latency or alive status, verify proxied egress IP through 7890, reload Clash config through the controller, or troubleshoot Clash/mihomo proxy selection.
4	---
5	
6	# Clash Proxy API
7	
8	Operate Clash/mihomo through its external-controller API without re-discovering controller details or hand-writing curl calls.
9	
10	## Quick Start
11	
12	Prefer the bundled helper for agent automation:
13	
14	```sh
15	python3 /home/taa/.agents/skills/clash-proxy-api/scripts/clash_api.py status
16	python3 /home/taa/.agents/skills/clash-proxy-api/scripts/clash_api.py groups
17	python3 /home/taa/.agents/skills/clash-proxy-api/scripts/clash_api.py delay "Hanru Azure (JP)"
18	python3 /home/taa/.agents/skills/clash-proxy-api/scripts/clash_api.py switch PROXY "Hanru Azure (JP)"
19	python3 /home/taa/.agents/skills/clash-proxy-api/scripts/clash_api.py egress --proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890
20	```
21	
22	The helper resolves the controller from:
23	
24	1. `CLASH_CONTROLLER` and optional `CLASH_SECRET`
25	2. This host's Television integration: `~/.config/television/clash-source.sh controller`
26	3. A reachable fallback at `127.0.0.1:9090`
27	
28	It sends `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` when a secret is available and handles URL encoding for proxy/group names.
29	
30	## Default Workflow
31	
32	1. Run `status` first. Record the controller, version, important proxy group selections, and whether the target node appears in any group.
33	2. If switching to a named node, run `delay "<node name>"` before switching. If the delay test fails, report that and avoid switching unless the user explicitly asked to try anyway.
34	3. Switch the intended selector group with `switch <group> "<node name>"`. For this machine, the main group is commonly `PROXY`; `Final` and `GlobalMedia` often point at `PROXY`.
35	4. Run `status` again and verify the selected group changed.
36	5. If the user cares about actual traffic, run `egress --proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890` and summarize the observed IP, city, country, and org.
37	
38	For a request like "can 7890 switch to hanru, it is probably david now", resolve the exact case-sensitive node name from `status` or `groups`, test it, then switch `PROXY` to that node. Do not switch `Auto Select` unless the user specifically asks; URL-test groups may reselect automatically.
39	
40	## Interactive Local Tools
41	
42	This host also has Television channels:
43	
44	```sh
45	tv clash
46	tv clash-api
47	```
48	
49	Those are useful for a human picker UI. For non-interactive agent work, use the bundled helper or direct controller API calls.
50	
51	Relevant local files:
52	
53	- `~/.config/television/cable/clash-api.toml`
54	- `~/.config/television/clash-source.sh`
55	- `~/.config/television/clash-preview.sh`
56	- `~/.config/television/clash-switch.sh`
57	
58	## Direct API Shape
59	
60	Use direct curl only when the helper is insufficient:
61	
62	```sh
63	curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9090/version
64	curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9090/proxies
65	curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:9090/proxies/Hanru%20Azure%20%28JP%29/delay?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.gstatic.com%2Fgenerate_204&timeout=5000"
66	curl -sS -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
67	  --data '{"name":"Hanru Azure (JP)"}' \
68	  http://127.0.0.1:9090/proxies/PROXY
69	```
70	
71	When a controller secret is configured, add:
72

## 2. scripts/clash_api.py

A single-file, stdlib-only (`argparse`, `json`, `os`, `subprocess`, `urllib`, `pathlib`) Python 3 helper. Shebang `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, executable. No external dependencies. Uses `from __future__ import annotations` and modern type hints (`tuple[str, str]`, `dict[str, Any]`), so it targets Python 3.9+.

**Module constants:**
```python
DEFAULT_DELAY_URL = "http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204"
DEFAULT_EGRESS_URL = "https://ipinfo.io/json"
TV_SOURCE = Path.home() / ".config" / "television" / "clash-source.sh"
```

**Error type:** `class ClashError(RuntimeError)`. In `main()`, `ClashError` is caught and printed as `error: <msg>` to stderr with exit code 1. Any other exception (e.g. the `cmd_egress` network call) is NOT caught and would traceback.

### Controller discovery — `resolve_controller` (load-bearing, quoted verbatim):
```python
def resolve_controller(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:
    if args.controller:
        return strip_scheme(args.controller), args.secret or ""

    env_controller = os.environ.get("CLASH_CONTROLLER", "").strip()
    env_secret = os.environ.get("CLASH_SECRET", "").strip()
    if env_controller:
        return strip_scheme(env_controller), env_secret

    if TV_SOURCE.exists() and os.access(TV_SOURCE, os.X_OK):
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [str(TV_SOURCE), "controller"],
                text=True,
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                timeout=2,
                check=False,
            )
            lines = proc.stdout.splitlines()
            if lines and lines[0].strip():
                secret = lines[1].strip() if len(lines) > 1 else ""
                return strip_scheme(lines[0].strip()), secret
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            pass

    return "127.0.0.1:9090", ""
```
Precedence: `--controller` flag → `CLASH_CONTROLLER`/`CLASH_SECRET` env → the Television `clash-source.sh controller` subprocess (expects line 1 = controller, line 2 = secret; 2s timeout, failures silently swallowed) → hardcoded `127.0.0.1:9090` with no secret. Note `--secret` is only honored on the `--controller` branch; when the controller comes from env, `--secret` is ignored (env secret wins).

**`strip_scheme`** normalizes a URL/host to bare `host:port`:
```python
def strip_scheme(value: str) -> str:
    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(value)
    if parsed.scheme and parsed.netloc:
        return parsed.netloc
    return value.removeprefix("http://").removeprefix("https://").rstrip("/")
```

### HTTP core — `request_json` (load-bearing, quoted verbatim):
```python
def request_json(host, secret, method, endpoint, *, payload=None, timeout=5):
    url = f"http://{host}/{endpoint.lstrip('/')}"
    data = None
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
    if secret:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {secret}"
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            body = resp.read()
            return resp.status, decode_json(body)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        body = exc.read()
        return exc.code, decode_json(body)
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        raise ClashError(f"controller {host} unreachable: {exc.reason}") from exc
```
Always uses `http://` (never https) to reach the controller. HTTP >=300 is returned as `(status, data)` for the caller to handle; connection failures become `ClashError`. `decode_json` returns `None` for empty bodies, parsed JSON, or the raw text if JSON parsing fails.

**Shared helpers:**
- `get_proxies(host, secret)` — `GET /proxies`, raises on HTTP>=300 or unexpected payload, returns the `proxies` dict.
- `selector_items(proxies)` — filters to entries that have a list `"all"` field (i.e. selectable groups), returns sorted `[(name, value)]`.

### CLI interface (`build_parser`)

Global flags: `--controller` (host:port or URL), `--secret`. Subcommand is **required** (`dest="command", required=True`). Six subcommands:

| Command | Args | Endpoint(s) hit | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|

Prints a **preferred/hardcoded ordering** first: `["PROXY", "Final", "GlobalMedia", "HKMTMedia", "Auto Select", "GLOBAL"]`, then remaining selectors. Each line via `print_group`: `- <name>: now=<now> type=<type> alive=<alive> members=<count>`. |
| `groups` | `--members` | `GET /proxies` | Lists selectable groups as `name\tnow=..\ttype=..`; with `--members` also prints each member indented. |
| `proxies` | `--filter <substr>` | `GET /proxies` | Lists leaf proxies (everything NOT a selector group), case-insensitive substring filter; line format `name\ttype=..\talive=..\tudp=..`. |
| `delay` | `proxy` (positional), `--url` (default gstatic 204), `--timeout-ms` (default 5000) | `GET /proxies/<url-encoded-name>/delay?url=..&timeout=..` | URL-encodes the proxy name with `quote(..., safe="")`; request timeout = `timeout_ms/1000 + 2`. Prints raw JSON response. |
| `switch` | `group`, `proxy` (both positional) | `GET /proxies` (validation) then `PUT /proxies/<url-encoded-group>` with `{"name": proxy}` | **Pre-validates**: group must exist and be selectable, and `proxy` must be in `group["all"]`, else `ClashError`. On success prints `switched <group> -> <proxy>`. |
| `egress` | `--proxy` (default `http://127.0.0.1:7890`), `--url` (default `https://ipinfo.io/json`), `--timeout` (default 10) | External URL through the local proxy (NOT the controller) | Builds a `ProxyHandler` opener with `{"http": proxy, "https": proxy}`, fetches the URL, pretty-prints JSON. This call is outside the `ClashError` handling, so network failures raise an uncaught traceback. |

**`cmd_switch` quoted verbatim** (the validation is the load-bearing safety logic):
```python
def cmd_switch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    host, secret = resolve_controller(args)
    proxies = get_proxies(host, secret)
    group = proxies.get(args.group)
    if not isinstance(group, dict) or not isinstance(group.get("all"), list):
        raise ClashError(f"group not found or not selectable: {args.group}")
    if args.proxy not in group["all"]:
        raise ClashError(f"proxy {args.proxy!r} is not a member of group {args.group!r}")

    encoded_group = urllib.parse.quote(args.group, safe="")
    status, data = request_json(host, secret, "PUT", f"proxies/{encoded_group}",
        payload={"name": args.proxy}, timeout=5)
    if status >= 300:
        raise ClashError(f"switch failed with HTTP {status}: {data}")
    print(f"switched {args.group} -> {args.proxy}")
    return 0
```

**Endpoints used overall:** `GET /version`, `GET /proxies`, `GET /proxies/<name>/delay`, `PUT /proxies/<group>`. No `/configs` (reload), `/connections`, `/rules`, `/traffic`, or `/logs` endpoints are implemented.

    print(f"switched {args.group} -&gt; {args.proxy}")
    return 0
```

**OS-specific logic:** None on the surface — it's pure stdlib and works cross-platform. The only OS/host coupling is the Television `clash-source.sh` discovery path under `~/.config/television/`, which is a personal/Linux-host convention, and the `/home/taa/...` path in SKILL.md.

**Endpoints used overall:** `GET /version`, `GET /proxies`, `GET /proxies/&lt;name&gt;/delay`, `PUT /proxies/&lt;group&gt;`. No `/configs` (reload), `/connections`, `/rules`, `/traffic`, or `/logs` endpoints are implemented.

It's an OpenAI-style agent-launcher descriptor: display name, one-line description, and a `default_prompt` that references the skill via `$clash-proxy-api`. No model config, tools list, or other logic.

## Summary of notable imperfections / coupling

- **Hardcoded non-portable path** in SKILL.md Quick Start: `/home/taa/.agents/skills/...` (won't match this repo location `/Users/david/.../skills/local/clash-proxy-api/`, and is a Linux home path on a macOS host).
- **Host-specific baked-in knowledge**: node names "Hanru"/"David", group names `PROXY`/`Final`/`GlobalMedia`/`HKMTMedia`/`Auto Select`, and Television integration files — all specific to one machine, not generic.
- **Description promises "reload Clash config"** but no reload/`/configs` command exists in the script.
- **`--secret` flag is partially ignored** — only applied when `--controller` is also given; env-discovered secret cannot be overridden by `--secret`.
- **`egress` errors are uncaught** (outside the `ClashError` handler) — a proxy/network failure produces a raw traceback rather than a clean `error:` message.
- **Controller is always contacted over `http://`** (no https support), consistent with the local-controller assumption.</result>

# Clash / mihomo tv helper scripts — analysis

All four helpers live in the chezmoi source dir (prefixed `executable_`) and render to `~/.config/television/` without the prefix. The channel invokes the **rendered** copies via `$HOME/.config/television/…`.

| Source (chezmoi) | Rendered (invoked) |
|---|---|
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_clash-source.sh` | `/Users/david/.config/television/clash-source.sh` |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_clash-preview.sh` | `/Users/david/.config/television/clash-preview.sh` |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_clash-switch.sh` | `/Users/david/.config/television/clash-switch.sh` |
| `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_clash-parse.py` | `/Users/david/.config/television/clash-parse.py` |

Channel config: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/clash-api.toml` (there is also a sibling `clash.toml` for the YAML-backed channel).

The important architectural fact: **`clash-parse.py` is the single source of truth for config-file discovery and YAML parsing**; the three shell scripts discover the live controller by shelling out to it (`clash-parse.py controller`) and then layering a reachability check + `127.0.0.1:9090` fallback on top. `clash-switch.sh` doesn't even do that itself — it re-uses `clash-source.sh controller`.

## 1. `clash-parse.py` — config discovery + YAML parsing (the core)

Shebang runs it via uv with an inline PEP 723 dep block (`PyYAML>=6.0`):
```
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
```
Invoked as `clash-parse.py <mode> [--kind K] [--name N] [--config PATH]`, modes: `proxies groups rules summary path yaml server controller groups-for-switch`.

### Config-file discovery

Two candidate-path builders. Runtime candidates (lines 36–47) — note the macOS-specific `Library/Application Support` entries and the clash-vs-mihomo split:
```python
def _runtime_candidate_paths() -> list[Path]:
    home = Path.home()
    paths: list[Path] = []
    for base in (
        home / ".config" / "clash",
        home / ".config" / "mihomo",
        home / "Library" / "Application Support" / "clash",
        home / "Library" / "Application Support" / "mihomo",
        ):
        for ext in ("config.yaml", "config.yml"):
            paths.append(base / ext)
    return paths
```

Active-profile resolution (lines 50–99) parses a Clash-Verge / Clash-for-Windows style `profiles/list.yml` that has a `files: []` array and an `index:` pointer, then resolves `files[index].time|file|path` to an absolute or `list.yml`-relative file (adding `.yml`/`.yaml` if the entry has no suffix):
```python
def _active_profile_path() -> Path | None:
    list_path = Path.home() / ".config" / "clash" / "profiles" / "list.yml"
    ...
    files = data.get("files")
    index = data.get("index")
    if not isinstance(files, list) or not isinstance(index, int) or not (0 <= index < len(files)):
        return None
    entry = files[index]
    ...
    raw_name = entry.get("time") or entry.get("file") or entry.get("path")
    ...
    candidate = Path(raw_name).expanduser()
    if candidate.is_absolute():
        return candidate if candidate.is_file() else None
    base = list_path.parent
    variants = [base / raw_name]
    if candidate.suffix not in {".yml", ".yaml"}:
        variants.extend((base / f"{raw_name}.yml", base / f"{raw_name}.yaml"))
    for variant in variants:
        ... return variant if is_file()
```

`find_config()` (lines 121–145) is what `proxies/groups/rules/summary/yaml/server/path` use. Note the deliberate security decision quoted in its docstring — an explicit `$CLASH_CONFIG` that doesn't exist is surfaced as an error and **never** falls back to common paths, to avoid picking up the wrong config and leaking a `secret:` in preview output:
```python
def find_config() -> tuple[Path | None, str | None]:
    env = os.environ.get("CLASH_CONFIG", "").strip()
    if env:
        p = Path(env).expanduser()
        try:
            if p.is_file():
                return p, None
        except OSError as e:
            return None, f"CLASH_CONFIG unreadable: {p} ({e})"
        return None, f"CLASH_CONFIG path not found: {p}"
    for p in _default_candidate_paths():   # active_profile first, then runtime candidates
        try:
            if p.is_file():
                return p, None
        except OSError:
            continue
    return None, "Set CLASH_CONFIG or place under ~/.config/clash/"
```
`_default_candidate_paths()` = active profile first, then the runtime candidates. Parsing is `yaml.safe_load` only, coerced to `{}` if not a dict (`load_config`, lines 147–150). It never writes back.

### Controller discovery inside the parser (`controller` subcommand)

`cmd_controller()` (lines 315–333) is the authoritative external-controller resolver. Precedence: **env → then a controller-specific config path override**. Crucially it does NOT use `find_config()`'s result directly for the final answer — it re-reads `_controller_config_path()` (which prefers the **runtime** `config.yaml` over the active subscription profile, because subscription profiles usually omit `external-controller`/`secret`):
```python
def cmd_controller(cfg: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    env_host = os.environ.get("CLASH_CONTROLLER", "").strip()
    env_secret = os.environ.get("CLASH_SECRET", "").strip()
    if env_host:
        return env_host, env_secret

    host = str(cfg.get("external-controller", "") or "")
    secret = env_secret or str(cfg.get("secret", "") or "")

    controller_path = _controller_config_path()
    if controller_path is not None:
        try:
            controller_cfg = load_config(controller_path)
        except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError):
            controller_cfg = {}
        if isinstance(controller_cfg, dict):
            host = str(controller_cfg.get("external-controller", "") or host)
            secret = env_secret or str(controller_cfg.get("secret", "") or secret)
    return str(host), str(secret)
```
with (lines 111–118):
```python
def _controller_config_path() -> Path | None:
    for p in _runtime_candidate_paths():   # runtime configs preferred here
        try:
            if p.is_file():
                return p
        except OSError:
            continue
    return _active_profile_path()
```
Output is exactly two lines to stdout: `host\nsecret\n` (empty lines when unknown — see `_emit_placeholder` `controller` branch, lines 354–356, which prints two blank lines). That two-line contract is what every shell caller reads.

Other subcommands relevant to the channel: `path` prints the resolved config path (used by the reload action); `server --name N` returns `server:port` for a proxy (used by latency TCP-probe fallback and copy-server); `groups-for-switch` (lines 336–346) emits only groups whose `type ∈ {select, fallback, url-test, load-balance}` as `group\tname\ttype\tmember | member | …`.

Rule parsing (`cmd_rules`, lines 207–225) splits comma strings, special-casing `MATCH` (no pattern). Proxy flags (`_proxy_flags`, lines 163–175) collect `tls/udp/network/cipher`.

## 2. `clash-source.sh` — the tv source emitter (+ `controller` shim)

Invoked by the channel as `clash-source.sh {api-proxies|api-groups|api-rules|api}` (clash-api.toml lines 35–40); also `api-groups-for-switch` (from switch) and `controller` (from switch/actions). YAML modes `proxies|groups|rules|summary` just delegate to `clash-parse.py`.

### Controller discovery (`resolve_controller`, lines 42–77)

Three tiers: env override → parser + reachability probe → `127.0.0.1:9090` probe (the "Docker/localhost" fallback). This is exposed verbatim to other scripts via the `controller` subcommand (lines 373–376 just call `resolve_controller`):
```bash
resolve_controller() {
  if [ -n "${CLASH_CONTROLLER:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CLASH_CONTROLLER" "${CLASH_SECRET:-}"
    return 0
  fi

  local host="" secret=""
  if ! parse_available; then
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
    else
      printf '\n\n'
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  {
    read -r host || true
    read -r secret || true
  } < <("$PARSE" controller 2>/dev/null || printf '\n\n')

  if [ -n "$host" ]; then
    local auth=()
    [ -n "$secret" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
  else
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"
  fi
}
```
Notes on the logic: `parse_available()` (lines 22–24) gates on `clash-parse.py` being executable **and** `uv` being on PATH — if uv is missing it skips YAML resolution entirely and only tries `127.0.0.1:9090`. The health check is always `GET /version`. Auth is `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` (built once in `prepare_controller`, lines 79–92). `base="http://$ctrl_host"`.

### Endpoints called

- `GET /version` — health probe (everywhere) and in `emit_api_summary` (line 256) for version/premium/meta tags.
- `GET /configs` — summary emits `port, socks-port, redir-port, mixed-port, tproxy-port, allow-lan, bind-address, ipv6, log-level, mode` (lines 283–312).
- `GET /connections` — summary emits connection count + `uploadTotal`/`downloadTotal` (lines 314–329).
- `GET /proxies` — feeds `api-proxies`, `api-groups`, `api-groups-for-switch` (leaf vs group split by presence of an `all: []` array; `now` = current selection; `history[-1].delay/meanDelay` for latency).
- `GET /rules` — feeds `api-rules`.

`api_get_json <endpoint> <timeout>` (lines 94–100) is the generic getter. Endpoints are passed **without** a leading slash and joined as `"$base/$endpoint"`.

---

## 3. `clash-preview.sh` — preview panes + latency

Invoked as `clash-preview.sh {api-main|latency|api-meta} <kind> <name>` (clash-api.toml lines 46–50). `<name>` is URL-encoded before being put in a path (`_urlencode`, lines 98–101, via `urllib.parse.quote(safe="")`).

### Controller discovery (`_controller`, lines 53–96)

Functionally identical 3-tier logic to `clash-source.sh`, but it checks `-x "$PARSE"` and `command -v uv` as two separate early-exit branches instead of one `parse_available`:
```bash
_controller() {
  if [ -n "${CLASH_CONTROLLER:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CLASH_CONTROLLER" "${CLASH_SECRET:-}"
    return 0
  fi
  local host="" secret=""
  if [ ! -x "$PARSE" ]; then
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
    else printf '\n\n'; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ...same 127.0.0.1:9090 probe...
    return 0
  fi
  { read -r host || true; read -r secret || true; } < <("$PARSE" controller 2>/dev/null || printf '\n\n')
  if [ -n "$host" ]; then
    local auth=()
    [ -n "$secret" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"; return 0
    fi
  fi
  if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
  else printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"; fi
}
```
`_api_request <endpoint> <timeout>` (lines 103–117) reads those two lines and issues the curl. (Minor quirk: it only adds the auth header when `ctrl_secret` is non-empty, same as elsewhere.)

### Endpoints called

- `api-main` (`_show_api_main`, lines 119–202): proxy/group → `GET /proxies/<urlencoded>`; rule → `GET /rules` (then picks index `#NNNN-1` in Python); `api` kind → `GET /version` (external-controller), `GET /connections` (connections/traffic), `GET /configs` (config.* keys, single-key projection).
- `latency` for a **proxy** (lines 382–444): the headline endpoint —
  ```
  GET http://$host/proxies/$encoded/delay?timeout=5000&url=http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204
  ```
  If the controller isn't reachable it falls back to a **direct TCP probe + ping** using `clash-parse.py server --name` to get `server:port`.
- `latency` for a **group** (lines 446–470): `GET /proxies/<urlencoded>`; if no controller, shows static YAML via `clash-parse.py yaml --kind group`.
- `api-meta` (`_show_api_meta`, lines 204–352): proxy → `GET /proxies` (find groups referencing it); group → `GET /proxies/<encoded>` (current/members/history); rule → `GET /rules` (±2 neighbors); api → `GET /configs` or `GET /connections`.

### OS/client-specific handling here

The ping fallback branches on `uname -s` because macOS `ping -W` is milliseconds while Linux is seconds (lines 435–440):
```bash
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
  ping -c 3 -W 2000 "$server" 2>&1 | tail -n 6
else
  ping -c 3 -W 2 "$server" 2>&1 | tail -n 6
fi
```
TCP probe uses `nc -z -w3` when available. Output rendering degrades gracefully: `bat` → else `cat`; `jq` → else `python3 -m json.tool` → else `cat` (`pretty_json`, lines 45–51).

---

## 4. `clash-switch.sh` — switch a group's selection (PUT)

Invoked as `clash-switch.sh api <kind> <proxy-name>` (clash-api.toml line 97, Alt+S). Guards: kind must be `proxy`, name non-empty, `fzf` present.

It has **no discovery of its own** — it reuses `clash-source.sh controller` (which is `resolve_controller`), then health-checks `GET /version` (lines 33–51):
```bash
{ read -r host || true; read -r secret || true; } < <("$SOURCE" controller 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then echo 'external-controller not set'; sleep 1; exit 0; fi
auth=()
[ -n "${secret:-}" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
if ! curl -sS --max-time 2 "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'Controller %s unreachable\n' "$host"; sleep 1; exit 0
fi
```
It lists switchable groups containing the proxy (`api` mode → `clash-source.sh api-groups-for-switch`; `yaml` mode → `clash-parse.py groups-for-switch`), lets the user pick one via fzf, then issues the switch:
```bash
encoded_group=$(python3 -c 'import sys, urllib.parse as u; print(u.quote(sys.argv[1], safe=""))' "$group")
payload=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.dumps({"name": sys.argv[1]}))' "$name")
rc=$(curl -sS -o "$out" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 4 -X PUT \
  "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$payload" \
  "http://$host/proxies/$encoded_group" 2>/dev/null || true)
```
So: **`PUT /proxies/<group>` with body `{"name": "<proxy>"}`**, success = HTTP 2xx. Temp output goes to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/clash-switch.out`.

---

## 5. Additional endpoints/handling in the channel TOML itself

`clash-api.toml` actions embed more controller calls (all reuse `clash-source.sh controller` for host/secret):
- Alt+C `close_connections`: **`DELETE /connections`** (confirm y/N) — lines 100–121.
- Alt+R `reload_config`: **`PUT /configs?force=true`** body `{"path": "<cfg_path>"}`, where `cfg_path` = `$CLASH_CONFIG` or `clash-parse.py path`; includes a guard that a remote controller (`$CLASH_CONTROLLER` set) reload requires `CLASH_CONFIG` because the path must be visible on the controller host — lines 123–164.
- Alt+D `open_dashboard`: opens `http://$host/ui` (or `https://yacd.haishan.me/` if no host).
- Ctrl+Y `copy_server` / Alt+Y `copy_name`: use `clash-parse.py server --name`.

Cross-platform helpers in the TOML: dashboard open uses `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `wslview` (WSL); clipboard uses `pbcopy` (macOS) / `wl-copy` (Wayland) / `xclip` (X11) / OSC-52 base64 escape as terminal fallback.

---

### Summary of the discovery contract a new skill would mirror

- **Controller (host, secret)** resolution order, everywhere: `$CLASH_CONTROLLER`/`$CLASH_SECRET` → local YAML `external-controller`+`secret` (via `clash-parse.py controller`, which itself prefers the runtime `config.yaml` over the active subscription profile) verified reachable by `GET /version` → `127.0.0.1:9090` if it answers `GET /version`. Auth is always `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`, base `http://<host>`, and the two-line `host\nsecret` stdout contract glues the shell scripts to the parser.
- **Config file** resolution order: `$CLASH_CONFIG` (explicit, no fallback on miss) → `~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml` active profile → `~/.config/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}` → `~/Library/Application Support/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}` (macOS).
- **Endpoints touched**: `GET /version`, `GET /configs`, `GET /connections`, `GET /proxies`, `GET /proxies/:name`, `GET /proxies/:name/delay?timeout=5000&url=http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204`, `GET /rules`; `PUT /proxies/:group` (`{"name":…}`), `PUT /configs?force=true` (`{"path":…}`), `DELETE /connections`; dashboard `/ui`. Proxy/group names are always `urllib.parse.quote(safe="")`-encoded into the path.
</output>

    env_secret = os.environ.get("CLASH_SECRET", "").strip()

```bash
resolve_controller() {
  if [ -n "${CLASH_CONTROLLER:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CLASH_CONTROLLER" "${CLASH_SECRET:-}"
    return 0
  fi

  local host="" secret=""
  if ! parse_available; then
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
    else
      printf '\n\n'
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  {
    read -r host || true
    read -r secret || true
  } < <("$PARSE" controller 2>/dev/null || printf '\n\n')

  if [ -n "$host" ]; then
    local auth=()
    [ -n "$secret" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
    if curl -sS --max-time 1 "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  if curl -sS --max-time 1 "http://127.0.0.1:9090/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n\n' "127.0.0.1:9090"
  else
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$host" "$secret"
  fi
}
```
Notes on the logic: `parse_available()` (lines 22–24) gates on `clash-parse.py` being executable **and** `uv` being on PATH — if uv is missing it skips YAML resolution entirely and only tries `127.0.0.1:9090`. The health check is always `GET /version`. Auth is `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` (built once in `prepare_controller`, lines 79–92). `base="http://$ctrl_host"`.

- `GET /connections` — summary emits connection count + `uploadTotal`/`downloadTotal` (lines 314–329).
- `GET /proxies` — feeds `api-proxies`, `api-groups`, `api-groups-for-switch` (leaf vs group split by presence of an `all: []` array; `now` = current selection; `history[-1].delay/meanDelay` for latency).

### OS/client-specific handling here

The ping fallback branches on `uname -s` because macOS `ping -W` is milliseconds while Linux is seconds (lines 435–440):
```bash
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
  ping -c 3 -W 2000 "$server" 2>&1 | tail -n 6
else
  ping -c 3 -W 2 "$server" 2>&1 | tail -n 6
fi
```
TCP probe uses `nc -z -w3` when available. Output rendering degrades gracefully: `bat` → else `cat`; `jq` → else `python3 -m json.tool` → else `cat` (`pretty_json`, lines 45–51).

## 4. `clash-switch.sh` — switch a group's selection (PUT)

Invoked as `clash-switch.sh api <kind> <proxy-name>` (clash-api.toml line 97, Alt+S). Guards: kind must be `proxy`, name non-empty, `fzf` present.

```bash

if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then echo 'external-controller not set'; sleep 1; exit 0; fi
auth=()
[ -n "${secret:-}" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
if ! curl -sS --max-time 2 "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

encoded_group=$(python3 -c 'import sys, urllib.parse as u; print(u.quote(sys.argv[1], safe=""))' "$group")
payload=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.dumps({"name": sys.argv[1]}))' "$name")

  "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

### Summary of the discovery contract a new skill would mirror

- **Controller (host, secret)** resolution order, everywhere: `$CLASH_CONTROLLER`/`$CLASH_SECRET` → local YAML `external-controller`+`secret` (via `clash-parse.py controller`, which itself prefers the runtime `config.yaml` over the active subscription profile) verified reachable by `GET /version` → `127.0.0.1:9090` if it answers `GET /version`. Auth is always `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`, base `http://<host>`, and the two-line `host\nsecret` stdout contract glues the shell scripts to the parser.
- **Config file** resolution order: `$CLASH_CONFIG` (explicit, no fallback on miss) → `~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml` active profile → `~/.config/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}` → `~/Library/Application Support/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}` (macOS).
- **Endpoints touched**: `GET /version`, `GET /configs`, `GET /connections`, `GET /proxies`, `GET /proxies/:name`, `GET /proxies/:name/delay?timeout=5000&url=http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204`, `GET /rules`; `PUT /proxies/:group` (`{"name":…}`), `PUT /configs?force=true` (`{"path":…}`), `DELETE /connections`; dashboard `/ui`. Proxy/group names are always `urllib.parse.quote(safe="")`-encoded into the path.

# Skill authoring conventions in this repo — reference report

## 1. `references/authoring-patterns.md` — key patterns

**Location:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author/references/authoring-patterns.md`

### Description "pushiness" (frontmatter)
- `description` is required, `<=1024` chars. **"Include both what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60 characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there."**
- Budget tiers: **Green 120-500 chars** ("Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat"), Yellow 501-900 ("Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body"), Orange 901-1024 ("close to hard loader limits"), **Red >1024** ("Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators").
- Commit checklist items: **"Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"), not just a one-line summary"** and **"Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred, <=1024 chars required."**

### Calibrated specificity ("Calibrating control")
- **"Match instruction specificity to task fragility, not to "we should be thorough"."**
- Be prescriptive when: **"The operation is destructive or has side effects"**, a specific sequence must hold (migration/release/deploy), or an external system requires exact format.
- The prescriptive trick: **"even when prescriptive, explain why. Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just see "DO NOT" in caps."**
- Give freedom when: **"Multiple valid approaches exist"**, output is judgment-driven, or **"You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out."** For a code-review-style list it notes: **"what to look for, not how to look for it. The agent picks the approach."**

### Defaults, not menus
- **"When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as escape hatches."** Good: "Use pdfplumber for text extraction. For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract." Bad: "You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on..."

### Procedures over declarations
- **"Teach the agent how to approach the class of problem, not what to produce for one instance."** The example contrasts a one-query SQL recipe (bad) vs a generalized "read schema → join via `_id` convention → apply filters → aggregate" procedure (good).
- Caveat: **"Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the approach should generalize."**

### Gotchas section
- **"Often the single highest-value section in a skill. Concrete corrections to mistakes the agent will make without being told. Not generic advice."**
- **"Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is that the agent reads them before hitting the situation — by the time it realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened."**
- Iteration tip: **"every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written all at once."**

### Output templates
- **"Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape."**
- **"Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in `assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`."**

### Plan-validate-execute (and validation loops)
- Validation loop pattern: **"do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed"** ("instruct the agent to validate and re-try, not "do your best and stop"").
- Plan-validate-execute: **"For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate plan artifact that gets validated before any side effects happen."** The value is the validate step: **"A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not found — available: ..." lets the agent self-correct before the destructive step."** And: **"This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod" failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo."**

### Progressive disclosure / context budget
- Three loading levels: frontmatter (always; 120-500 preferred, 1024 max), `SKILL.md` body (**"<500 lines, <5000 tokens"**), `references/*` + `assets/*` + `scripts/*` (on demand, unlimited).
- **"If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md` and reference them with load conditions ("Read X if Y happens"), not just "see X for details"."** Reason given: **"Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution."**
- Spend-tokens test: **"for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?" If no, cut it."**

### Checklists for multi-step workflows
- Use `- [ ]` checkboxes with dependency arrows to a script: **"The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit."**

### Commit checklist (final gate) — verbatim highlights
- "SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)"
- "Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just listed at the bottom"
- "Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)"
- "Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags"
- **"No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying why"**

## 2. `references/script-design.md` — agentic CLI script rules

**Location:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author/references/script-design.md`

Headline framing: **"the caller is an LLM that reads your stderr to decide what to do next. Optimize for that."**

### Structured stdout vs prose stderr
- **"Prefer JSON / CSV / TSV / NDJSON over whitespace-aligned columns. Structured output is parseable by both the agent and standard tools (`jq`, `cut`, `awk`)."**
- **"Separate data from diagnostics. Send structured data to stdout; send progress, warnings, debug logs to stderr. The agent can then `jq` stdout cleanly while still seeing diagnostics if it wants."**
- Bash convention given: `log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }` for diagnostics → stderr; `printf '{"status":"ok"}\n'` for data → stdout.

### Error message style
- Pattern: **"what was wrong + what was expected + what to try."** Bad: "Error: invalid input". Good: `Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table. Received: "xml"`.
- For "not found" errors: **"include the available alternatives in the message — this lets the agent self-correct without re-querying the system"** (e.g. "Available fields: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed.").

### `--help` and exit codes
- **"`--help` is the primary documentation. The agent reads `--help` to learn the script."** Should include usage, options, examples, and an exit-codes block.
- **"The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior."** Suggested code table: `0` success, `1` invalid args/usage, `2` required input missing/not found, `3` external system failure, `4` validation failed, `>=10` skill-specific.
- **No interactive prompts, ever:** "A script that calls `read`, `input()`, or any TTY prompt hangs indefinitely. There is no recovery." Accept input via flags/env/stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).

### PEP 723 (self-contained scripts)
- **"When a script needs dependencies, prefer inline declarations over a sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with one command and no setup."**
- Python form: shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` plus a `# /// script` block with `requires-python` and `dependencies`. Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html` — **"uv creates an isolated environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically."** For full reproducibility: `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py`.

### Dry-run / idempotency
- **"Agents retry. "Create if not exists" beats "create and fail on duplicate"."**
- **"Implement [`--dry-run`] as a real preview (show what would change), not a no-op."** (Sample output shows `[dry-run] Would deploy ...`.)
- Predictable output size: harnesses truncate past ~10-30K chars, so default to a summary/limit, offer `--offset`/`--limit`, or require `--output FILE`.

### Version pinning
- **"Always pin"** `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`: `uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .`, `npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .`, `pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .`. Unpinned **"silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change."** `@latest` only if the skill explicitly says it tracks upstream latest.

### Bash 3.2 subset (macOS)
- **"Stock macOS ships bash 3.2."** Avoid (with replacements): `mapfile -t` → `while IFS= read -r line; do arr+=("$line"); done`; `${var,,}`/`${var^^}` → `tr`; `[[ -v VAR ]]` → `[ "${VAR+x}" = "x" ]`; associative arrays `declare -A` → indexed array + key parser or Python; `wait -n` → `wait`; `&>` → `>file 2>&1`.
- Lead every script with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail` (explains `-u`/`-e`/`-o pipefail`). If bash 4+ is needed: switch to PEP 723 Python (recommended) or add an explicit `BASH_VERSINFO` version-check guard.

### One-off vs bundled
- **"If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, don't bundle a script — reference the tool directly."** Bundle when the invocation grows past ~3 flags/needs computed args, composes multiple tools, must be tested independently, or you want a stable interface. **"State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md`."**

# Skill authoring conventions in this repo — reference report

## 1. `references/authoring-patterns.md` — key patterns

**Location:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author/references/authoring-patterns.md`

### Description "pushiness" (frontmatter)
- `description` is required, `<=1024` chars. **"Include both what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60 characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there."**
- Budget tiers: **Green 120-500 chars** ("Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat"), Yellow 501-900 ("Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body"), Orange 901-1024 ("close to hard loader limits"), **Red >1024** ("Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators").
- Commit checklist items: **"Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"), not just a one-line summary"** and **"Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred, <=1024 chars required."**

### Calibrated specificity ("Calibrating control")
- **"Match instruction specificity to task fragility, not to "we should be thorough"."**
- Be prescriptive when: **"The operation is destructive or has side effects"**, a specific sequence must hold (migration/release/deploy), or an external system requires exact format.
- The prescriptive trick: **"even when prescriptive, explain why. Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just see "DO NOT" in caps."**
- Give freedom when: **"Multiple valid approaches exist"**, output is judgment-driven, or **"You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out."** For a code-review-style list it notes: **"what to look for, not how to look for it. The agent picks the approach."**

### Defaults, not menus
- **"When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as escape hatches."** Good: "Use pdfplumber for text extraction. For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract." Bad: "You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on..."

### Procedures over declarations
- **"Teach the agent how to approach the class of problem, not what to produce for one instance."** The example contrasts a one-query SQL recipe (bad) vs a generalized "read schema → join via `_id` convention → apply filters → aggregate" procedure (good).
- Caveat: **"Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the approach should generalize."**

### Gotchas section
- **"Often the single highest-value section in a skill. Concrete corrections to mistakes the agent will make without being told. Not generic advice."**
- **"Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is that the agent reads them before hitting the situation — by the time it realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened."**
- Iteration tip: **"every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written all at once."**

### Output templates
- **"Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape."**
- **"Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in `assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`."**

### Plan-validate-execute (and validation loops)
- Validation loop pattern: **"do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed"** ("instruct the agent to validate and re-try, not "do your best and stop"").
- Plan-validate-execute: **"For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate plan artifact that gets validated before any side effects happen."** The value is the validate step: **"A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not found — available: ..." lets the agent self-correct before the destructive step."** And: **"This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod" failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo."**

### Progressive disclosure / context budget
- Three loading levels: frontmatter (always; 120-500 preferred, 1024 max), `SKILL.md` body (**"<500 lines, <5000 tokens"**), `references/*` + `assets/*` + `scripts/*` (on demand, unlimited).
- **"If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md` and reference them with load conditions ("Read X if Y happens"), not just "see X for details"."** Reason given: **"Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution."**
- Spend-tokens test: **"for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?" If no, cut it."**

### Checklists for multi-step workflows
- Use `- [ ]` checkboxes with dependency arrows to a script: **"The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit."**

### Commit checklist (final gate) — verbatim highlights
- "SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)"
- "Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just listed at the bottom"
- "Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)"
- "Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags"
- **"No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying why"**

## 2. `references/script-design.md` — agentic CLI script rules

**Location:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author/references/script-design.md`

Headline framing: **"the caller is an LLM that reads your stderr to decide what to do next. Optimize for that."**

### Structured stdout vs prose stderr
- **"Prefer JSON / CSV / TSV / NDJSON over whitespace-aligned columns. Structured output is parseable by both the agent and standard tools (`jq`, `cut`, `awk`)."**
- **"Separate data from diagnostics. Send structured data to stdout; send progress, warnings, debug logs to stderr. The agent can then `jq` stdout cleanly while still seeing diagnostics if it wants."**
- Bash convention given: `log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }` for diagnostics → stderr; `printf '{"status":"ok"}\n'` for data → stdout.

### Error message style
- Pattern: **"what was wrong + what was expected + what to try."** Bad: "Error: invalid input". Good: `Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table. Received: "xml"`.
- For "not found" errors: **"include the available alternatives in the message — this lets the agent self-correct without re-querying the system"** (e.g. "Available fields: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed.").

### `--help` and exit codes
- **"`--help` is the primary documentation. The agent reads `--help` to learn the script."** Should include usage, options, examples, and an exit-codes block.
- **"The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior."** Suggested code table: `0` success, `1` invalid args/usage, `2` required input missing/not found, `3` external system failure, `4` validation failed, `>=10` skill-specific.
- **No interactive prompts, ever:** "A script that calls `read`, `input()`, or any TTY prompt hangs indefinitely. There is no recovery." Accept input via flags/env/stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).

### PEP 723 (self-contained scripts)
- **"When a script needs dependencies, prefer inline declarations over a sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with one command and no setup."**
- Python form: shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` plus a `# /// script` block with `requires-python` and `dependencies`. Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html` — **"uv creates an isolated environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically."** For full reproducibility: `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py`.

### Dry-run / idempotency
- **"Agents retry. "Create if not exists" beats "create and fail on duplicate"."**
- **"Implement [`--dry-run`] as a real preview (show what would change), not a no-op."** (Sample output shows `[dry-run] Would deploy ...`.)
- Predictable output size: harnesses truncate past ~10-30K chars, so default to a summary/limit, offer `--offset`/`--limit`, or require `--output FILE`.

### Version pinning
- **"Always pin"** `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`: `uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .`, `npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .`, `pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .`. Unpinned **"silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change."** `@latest` only if the skill explicitly says it tracks upstream latest.

### Bash 3.2 subset (macOS)
- **"Stock macOS ships bash 3.2."** Avoid (with replacements): `mapfile -t` → `while IFS= read -r line; do arr+=("$line"); done`; `${var,,}`/`${var^^}` → `tr`; `[[ -v VAR ]]` → `[ "${VAR+x}" = "x" ]`; associative arrays `declare -A` → indexed array + key parser or Python; `wait -n` → `wait`; `&>` → `>file 2>&1`.
- Lead every script with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail` (explains `-u`/`-e`/`-o pipefail`). If bash 4+ is needed: switch to PEP 723 Python (recommended) or add an explicit `BASH_VERSINFO` version-check guard.

### One-off vs bundled
- **"If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, don't bundle a script — reference the tool directly."** Bundle when the invocation grows past ~3 flags/needs computed args, composes multiple tools, must be tested independently, or you want a stable interface. **"State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md`."**

## 3. `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — repo-specific rules

**Location:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author/references/this-repo-conventions.md`

- **Layout:** `skills/local/<name>/` for skills authored here (with `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`); `skills/vendor/<name>/` for cherry-picked upstream. **"New skills authored here go in `skills/local/`. Always."** **"Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`."**
- **Discovery symlink farms:** `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at repo root are **"active discovery-symlink farms, not legacy"** — relative symlinks (`../../skills/local/<name>`) so Cursor/Codex/Warp/OpenCode and Claude Code can dogfood. **"never add new canonical skill content directly under them."** `scripts/new-skill.sh` creates these symlinks in LOCAL mode.
- **Placement scopes** for `new-skill.sh`: LOCAL (default in this repo; canonical in `skills/local/<name>/`, or `skills/vendor/` with `--vendor`), PROJECT (canonical in `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/`), GLOBAL (rooted at `$HOME`). Fan-out rule: **"claude-code always, others only if their config root already exists at the base dir"**; the script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
- **Discovery depth:** the CLI scans one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels. **"Don't nest a skill more than 5 levels deep or it becomes invisible."**
- **Script mirroring:** some scripts are bundled in a skill AND mirrored to root `scripts/`. **"Mirrors must stay byte-identical. If you edit one, run the equivalent `cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no automated check for this — be careful."**
- **Docs to update when adding a local skill:** (1) a row in `docs/skills/index.md`, (2) a `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page, (3) a nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`, (4) a row in the README's "What's in here" table.
- **Project memory:** repo uses `project-knowledge-harness` on itself — `TODO.md` (validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`), `backlog/inbox.md`, `backlog/<slug>.md`, `pitfalls/<slug>.md`. **"When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to `pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history."**
- **`AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`** — edit either, don't replace the symlink.
- **Bash:** **"All bundled scripts must be bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS)."**
- **Conflict resolution:** **"When they conflict, this file wins for skills authored in this repo."** Notable local overrides:
  - **"We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on ad-hoc `uvx` invocations"** (so helpers compose with the `Makefile`/CI).
  - **"We use Bash for orchestration scripts ... PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or parsing-heavy helpers."**
  - **"Skill descriptions in this repo lean even pushier than the agentskills.io guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai."**

Short answer: you can PATCH the config to set the tun block (e.g. tun.enable = true), but enabling TUN usually requires restarting the Mihomo/Clash core (the UI normally does this for you). Sources below show the API endpoints, the tun config fields, and the common restart requirement. ([birkhofflee.github.io](https://birkhofflee.github.io/clash/runtime/external-controller.html))

Example workflow (adjust host:port and secret to your setup)

1) Confirm external-controller is enabled and you know the bind address and secret (API uses Authorization: Bearer <secret>). ([birkhofflee.github.io](https://birkhofflee.github.io/clash/runtime/external-controller.html))

2) Patch the runtime config to enable tun (example JSON):
curl -X PATCH "http://127.0.0.1:9090/configs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_SECRET>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tun":{"enable":true,"stack":"mixed","auto-route":true,"auto-detect-interface":true}}'

The external-controller supports PATCH /configs to update fields; the tun config keys and their meanings (enable, stack, auto-route, etc.) are documented in the mihomo / tun docs. ([birkhofflee.github.io](https://birkhofflee.github.io/clash/runtime/external-controller.html))

3) Restart the core so the TUN device and routing are actually created (most UIs do this automatically). You can call the API restart endpoint:
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:9090/restart" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_SECRET>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

Mihomo exposes a /restart endpoint and many frontends update the config then restart the core because enabling TUN requires the core to re-create the virtual interface. ([wiki.metacubex.one](https://wiki.metacubex.one/en/api/?utm_source=openai))

Notes and tips
- Use the actual external-controller bind (some builds use 9097 or other ports); check your config.yaml. ([birkhofflee.github.io](https://birkhofflee.github.io/clash/runtime/external-controller.html))  
- Some tun options (e.g., stack, dns-hijack, auto-redirect) have platform-specific requirements (admin/root, firewall rules, driver install). Read the tun docs for the keys you set. ([wiki.metacubex.one](https://wiki.metacubex.one/en/config/inbound/tun/))

74	-H "Authorization: Bearer $CLASH_SECRET"
75	```
76	
77	## Safety Notes
78	
79	- Treat `PUT /proxies/<group>` as a live runtime change. It is normally reversible, but it can affect ongoing downloads, uploads, browser sessions, and other tools using `http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, or `all_proxy`.
80	- Avoid editing Clash YAML or reloading config unless the user asks. Switching a selector group is usually enough.
81	- Do not expose secrets in final answers. Mention that a secret was used, not its value.
82	- If an upload or other long-running job is already using `127.0.0.1:7890`, note that switching the group may change that job's route.

```md
# Plan: Make `clash-proxy-api` a genuinely useful, multi-client Clash/mihomo control skill

## Context

`skills/local/clash-proxy-api/` was bootstrapped by Codex. It works but is narrow and
machine-specific: it only wraps the controller API for `status/groups/proxies/delay/switch/egress`,
hardcodes one host's assumptions (`/home/taa/...` path, `127.0.0.1:9090` + port `7890`, node names
`Hanru`/`David`, group `PROXY`), has no `## Gotchas` / `## Available scripts` sections, promises
"reload config" it never implements, and lets `egress` traceback on network errors.

The goal is a skill you can talk to naturally — *"what's my current node?"*, *"switch to the JP node"*,
*"am I in global or rule mode?"*, *"turn on TUN"*, *"reload my config"*, *"the API isn't working, how do I
turn it on?"*, *"there's no system-proxy toggle on my Ubuntu box"* — that **adapts to the OS and client**.

Research corrected two load-bearing assumptions:
- **The controller is not always `127.0.0.1:9090`.** Clash Verge Rev defaults to `127.0.0.1:9097`
  (proxy ports `7897/7898`). The skill must *discover* the controller, never hardcode it.
- **Clash for Windows is dead** (repo deleted ~late 2023). Current landscape: **mihomo core/CLI**,
  **Clash Verge Rev** (GUI, mainstream CFW replacement), **ClashX / ClashX Meta** (macOS), plus
  mihomo-party / FlClash. `PATCH /configs` *can* set `mode`/`tun`/`allow-lan` at runtime, but enabling
  TUN usually needs a core `/restart` **and** elevated privileges (Service Mode).

### Assumed scope (user stepped away during clarification — adjust at approval)
1. **Control scope:** API control **plus** OS system-proxy toggling (macOS `networksetup` / GNOME
   `gsettings`), guarded by `--dry-run`/confirm — this is the explicit "Ubuntu has no toggle" gap.
   Mixin/config-file edits stay as *guidance*, not automation.
2. **First-class clients:** mihomo core/CLI, Clash Verge Rev, ClashX/ClashX Meta; remote/router/Docker
   via `CLASH_CONTROLLER`/`CLASH_SECRET` env.
3. **Repo wiring:** full integration (marketplace + docs + README).

## Design principles

- **Self-contained + portable.** `clash_api.py` stays `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, **stdlib-only** (no `uv`
  dependency for the core — `python3` is far likelier present downstream). Optional `import yaml` if
  available; otherwise a light regex scan for the two top-level keys we need.
- **Discover, never hardcode.** Reuse the proven discovery contract from the user's TV helper
  `~/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_clash-parse.py` (`cmd_controller`,
  `_runtime_candidate_paths`, `_active_profile_path`, the `$CLASH_CONFIG` set-but-missing-is-an-error
  rule) by **porting** that logic into the skill's own script.
- Structured summary to **stdout**, diagnostics to **stderr**, `--help` with examples + exit codes,
  `--dry-run` on every mutating op. Bash scripts target **bash 3.2**.

## Files to change / add

### 1. Rewrite `scripts/clash_api.py` (stdlib-only, portable)

**Controller discovery** (replace `resolve_controller`, keep it as the reliable core):
1. `--controller` (+ `--secret` — fix current bug where `--secret` is ignored unless `--controller` is set).
2. `CLASH_CONTROLLER` / `CLASH_SECRET` env.
3. Optional TV hook: `~/.config/television/clash-source.sh controller` (keep as bonus, guarded).
4. **Local config parse** (ported from `clash-parse.py`): `$CLASH_CONFIG` (error, no fallback, if set-but-missing)
   → `~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml` active profile → `~/.config/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}`
   → macOS `~/Library/Application Support/{clash,mihomo, clash-verge-rev app dirs}/…`. Prefer the runtime
   `config.yaml` over subscription profiles (they usually omit `external-controller`/`secret`). Read
   `external-controller` + `secret` via optional PyYAML or a regex scan of those top-level keys.
5. Probe common defaults in order: `127.0.0.1:9090`, then `127.0.0.1:9097` (Verge Rev), via `GET /version`.
6. All fail → structured error (exit `3`) listing what was tried, pointing at `doctor` + the enable-API reference.

**Subcommands** (extend; drop hardcoded `preferred` group list and Hanru/David/PROXY specifics):
- `status` — controller, secret yes/no, version (+ meta/premium), **mode + tun + ports from `GET /configs`**, then generic selector-group list (`GLOBAL` last, else alpha).
- `config get` — `GET /configs`.
- `mode <rule|global|direct>` — `PATCH /configs {"mode":…}`.
- `tun <on|off> [--restart]` — `PATCH /configs {"tun":{"enable":…}}`; warn re: privileges/Service Mode; `--restart` → `POST /restart`.
- `allow-lan <on|off>` — `PATCH /configs`.
- `reload [--path P] [--dry-run]` — `PUT /configs?force=true {"path":…}` (implements the long-promised reload).
- `connections [--json]` / `connections close [--id X | --all --yes]` — `GET`/`DELETE /connections[/:id]`.
- `rules [--filter]` — `GET /rules`.
- `groups [--members]`, `proxies [--filter]` — keep.
- `delay <proxy>` — keep; parse+print delay clearly. `group-delay <group>` — `GET /group/:name/delay` (mihomo, test all members).
- `switch <group> <proxy>` — keep validation (group selectable + proxy is a member).
- `egress` — **fix**: wrap network errors as `ClashError` (exit `3`); default proxy derived from discovered `mixed-port`/`port` (fallback `7890`).
- `doctor` — probe discovery, report what was found/tried, detect OS + likely client (scan config dirs / running procs), and on failure point to the exact client's steps in the enable-API reference. Powers *"turn the API on for me."*
- Global: `--json` opt-in on query cmds; `--help` epilog with **exit codes** (`0` ok, `1` usage, `2` group/proxy not found, `3` controller unreachable, `4` op rejected).

### 2. Add `scripts/clash_sysproxy.sh` (bash 3.2) — OS system-proxy toggle
`detect` | `on <host:port>` | `off`, `--dry-run` (real preview) + confirm/`--yes`:
- macOS: `networksetup -set{web,securewebproxy,socksfirewall}proxy` / `-setwebproxystate off` on the active service (resolved via `-listnetworkserviceorder`).
- GNOME/Ubuntu: `gsettings set org.gnome.system.proxy mode 'manual'|'none'` + host/port keys.
- Always also print `export http_proxy/https_proxy/all_proxy` lines (can't mutate parent shell).
- No `networksetup`/`gsettings` → print env-var approach + reference pointer. `--help`, exit codes, prose→stderr.

### 3. Add `references/` (loaded on demand)
- `references/enable-api-by-client.md` — the research deliverable. Per **client × OS**: how to turn on
  `external-controller`, its default address/port/secret, and where **System Proxy / TUN / Service Mode /
  Mixin** live. Covers mihomo core/CLI, Clash Verge Rev (`:9097`, Service Mode for TUN, Merge/Extend for
  Mixin), ClashX/ClashX Meta, mihomo-party/FlClash (pointers), legacy CFW (discontinued → migrate), and
  remote/OpenClash/Docker (`CLASH_CONTROLLER` env). *Verify current details against the mihomo wiki +
  Clash Verge Rev repo during implementation.*
- `references/api-endpoints.md` — full endpoint catalog (methods/payloads) incl. the streaming ones the
